units.text: EXT. CRANBERRY BOG - BEFORE DAWN
A flooded harvest bog, a rectangle of black water under a sky the color of dishwater.
Ten thousand red berries float on the surface, a drifting crimson carpet corralled by yellow booms.
Mist moves in low skeins.
Far off a pump engine thumps.
VIVIAN KESTREL, 40s, in chest waders and a stolen foreman's jacket, wades waist-deep through the berries with a dry bag held overhead.
The berries part around her and close again behind, leaving no wake.
She moves like a woman who has learned that patience is a kind of weight.
She stops at the center of the bog.
She looks at the sky, then at the far levee, and mutters.
Come on. Come on, you old goat.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Nothing answers.
A heron lifts from the reeds and flaps away.
She waits, and sweat runs down her temple though the water is cold.
A pair of headlights crawl along the levee road, a mile out.
They slow, stop, go dark.
A door shuts.
The pump engine stutters and cuts out and the silence is sudden and total.
Twelve minutes, I told you. Twelve.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: A figure picks his way down the levee bank, flashlight beam bouncing.
LEOPOLD ASANTE, 60s, heavy, in a tweed coat that has no business in a bog, slides on the last six feet of mud and lands on his hands.
The flashlight goes in the water.
It sinks glowing, shrinks, and vanishes.
That was a good flashlight.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: You were supposed to come alone.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: I came alone. The flashlight was a second guest.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: He wades out, holding his coat above the waterline with both fists, grimacing at every step.
The berries bump his knees.
At ten feet he stops, breathing hard.
You have it?
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: I have what you paid for.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: That's not an answer.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: It's the only one you get until I see the envelope.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: He reaches into the coat.
Takes out a plastic freezer bag, fat with cash, and holds it up.
The bag shines dull yellow in the thin light.
She lowers the dry bag and unzips the top.
For a moment neither moves.
Then Vivian's hand goes into the bag and Leopold's hand goes deeper into his coat, and both of them stop at once, because somewhere on the levee a dog barks.
Whose dog?
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Not mine.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: Whose dog, Leopold?
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: I don't know! Farmers have dogs!
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: The barking intensifies, joined by a second dog.
Headlights flick on at the levee's far end, then another pair behind.
Vivian sees them first.
She throws the dry bag at Leopold, who catches it against his chest and goes down backward into the berries, which close over him in a red bloom.
Stupid, stupid, stupid.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: She grabs his collar, hauls him up streaming and spitting, and shoves the freezer bag into her jacket.
He struggles against her and they turn together in the berries, grappling, her elbow in his ribs, his knee in the water, until she plants a boot and pulls him bodily toward the reeds.
They crash through the booms, scattering a hundred yards of floating berries, and fall into the sedge on the far side of the bog with the dry bag between them.
You pushed me.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: I saved you.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: You pushed me in a bog.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: It's a saving push.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: The dogs reach the water's edge and stop, baying.
Flashlights sweep the surface.
A man's voice calls, indistinct, bored, tired.
Leopold and Vivian lie flat in the sedge, shoulder to shoulder, not breathing, mud on their faces, red berries stuck in their hair like ornaments.
The flashlights linger.
A long minute.
Then a truck door slams, an engine starts, and the headlights draw away down the levee.
The two lie still a while longer.
The mist closes in.
The first thin light comes across the water and turns the berries to coral.
We'll never do this again.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: No.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: It was a bad idea.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: The worst.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: She sits up and unzips the dry bag.
Inside is a small velvet case.
She opens it, and the dawn catches whatever is in there, a cold white fire, and for the first time that morning Vivian smiles.
Is it all right?
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: It's perfect.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: Leopold takes the freezer bag from her jacket, unsealed, and counts the bills with wet fingers.
A berry has got into the bag.
He fishes it out and eats it.
Tart.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: They always are.
units.name: VIVIAN

units.text: She closes the case.
He holds out his hand and she shakes it, solemn, absurd, both of them red to the elbows.
Then they stand and wade away in opposite directions through the drifting fruit.
